IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NOS.               OF 2026
(@SLP(CRL.) NOS. 14771-14772 OF 2026)
RAMSUNDER CHOUHAN AND ANR. ETC.  ..... APPELLANT(S)
              VERSUS
STATE OF CHHATTISGARH ..... RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Heard.
2. Leave granted.
3. The appellants were visited with an FIR No.293/2023 by PS Sitapur for the
offence under Section 20(b)(ii)(B) of the  Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic
Substances  Act,  1985  (NDPS  Act) .  On  completion  of  investigation,
chargesheet has been filed and charges were framed under Section 20(b)(ii)
(B) of the NDPS Act. After trial they came to be convicted on 17.01.2025 and
each of the accused was sentenced to 5 years RI and fine of Rs.25,000/-
with six months RI as default sentence. Criminal Appeal Nos. 217/2025 and
455/2025 filed on behalf of the appellants herein came to be disposed of by
upholding the conviction and the sentence was reduced from 5 years to 3
years and the fine imposed was maintained. Hence, these appeals.
4. Having heard the learned counsels appearing for the parties, we do not
find  any  good  ground  to  entertain  the  appeals  insofar  as  conviction  is
1                                                                    SLP(CRL.) NOS. 14771-14772 OF 2026

--- Page 269 ---
concerned.  However,  having  regard  to  the  fact  that  quantity  of  the
contraband  seized  was  less  than  the  commercial  quantity  and  even
otherwise the prosecution has alleged that together the accused persons
were in joint possession of 19.100 kg of Ganja, the sentence of 2 years 1
month which they have already undergone would suffice and we hope and
trust by this time the appellants would have been reformed and would not
indulge in similar acts in future. As such, the sentence of three years which
has  been  awarded  by  the  High  Court  is  modified  to  the  one  already
undergone and the appellants are ordered to be released forthwith, if not
required in any other case.
5. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent-State shall intimate the
jurisdictional Jail where the appellants have been lodged and undergoing the
sentence of the order.
6. With aforesaid modification of the sentence the appeals stand allowed in
part.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

(ARAVIND KUMAR)

(VIPUL M. PANCHOLI)

4. The relevant part of the non reportable judgment is as
under:-
“24.   ..... we are of the opinion that just as in the
decision in Ujaas Energy Ltd. 6, the appellant should
be permitted to raise a counterclaim for the sole
purpose of claiming set-off and the appellant would
not derive any positive or affirmative relief of
recovery on the basis of the counterclaim. However, in
the more compelling circumstance of the SRA, being the
very erstwhile promoters of the CD, who accepted the
claim of the OC, in the CIRP with a major haircut by a
Resolution Plan, the SRA is deemed to have accepted
the  entire  claim  of  the  appellant/OC.  In  the
arbitration  constituted,  after  considering  the
monetary  claim  raised  by  the  respondent/SRA,  the
Arbitration Tribunal shall allow set-off to the extent
of the entire claim raised by the appellant, before
the RP in the CIRP, accepted in toto by the SRA in its
resolution plan, favoured with a majority of the CoC
and approved by the NCLT. 
25. The impugned order is sustained with only the
above  modification  that  the  appellant  would  be

--- Page 290 ---
entitled to raise the counterclaim as specified above
only for the purpose of set-off. If any amounts are
found due by the Arbitration Tribunal to be paid by
the appellant to the respondent then there shall be a
set-off to the extent of the entire counterclaim as
put forth by the appellant. Even in the extreme event
of the claim of the respondent being found untenable
in toto the appellant cannot seek any payment on the
basis  of  such  award  since  his  claim  stands
extinguished as against the CD and the SRA. The
benefit granted of the set-off, is only to ensure
equity and further the process of preservation of
assets of CD in the hands of the SRA, within the
contours of the IBC.  Needless to observe that the
issue  raised  by  the  respondent  regarding  the
encashment of the bank guarantee furnished by the
respondent, whether it was proper or improper, shall
also be considered by the Arbitration Tribunal.  
5. Pending application(s), if any, stands disposed of.

2. The petitioner calls in question the correctness of

of Madhya Pradesh Principal Seat at Jabalpur in MCRLC No.
19162/2026. By the said order, the High Court dismissed
the  regular  bail  application  of  the  petitioner  in
connection  with  Crime  No.RC0081995A014  registered  at
Police Station CBI, ACB, Bhopal, District Bhopal, Madhya
Pradesh for the offence punishable under Sections 420,
120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 13(1)(d)
and 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

submits that the petitioner has been in custody since 13 th
February,  2026  i.e.  for  the  last  nearly  8  months.

under Section 420 and is Magistrate triable.

respondent-State vehemently opposes the  prayer of the

absconding for a very long time and out of the other
accused  who  underwent  trial,  two  have  already  been
acquitted and two have been convicted and sentenced to
undergo imprisonment for 2½ years.
          SLP (Criminal) No.13774/2026                                                          Page 2 of 3

--- Page 293 ---
5. Considering the overall facts and circumstances, we
are inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail, pending
trial.  However, considering the past conduct of the
petitioner, the Trial Court may impose such conditions as
to ensure that he does not flee justice. Among the usual
conditions, the Trial Court shall include the following:
(i) The  petitioner  shall  surrender  his
passport;
(ii) The petitioner shall file on affidavit
giving the current address where he resides and
his contact number/mobile number; and
(iii) The petitioner shall file an undertaking
that he will not change his address and if he
changes, he will inform the concerned Court and
the prosecutor.

pending trial.

                             O R D E R
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the matter,

--- Page 316 ---
2
being a family affair, be referred to mediation so that a permanent
solution can be worked out between the parties especially in view
of a child being born to the petitioner and the respondent no.1,
who is the respondent no.2 in the present proceedings.
3. Accordingly, as prayed for, the matter is referred to the
Supreme Court Mediation Centre (SCMC).
4. Parties to initially appear before the Coordinator of the SCMC
on 28.10.2026 at 02:30 p.m. through virtual mode.
5. Thereafter, the learned Mediator shall take a call with regard
to whether the parties are required to appear physically.
6. However, if respondent no.1-wife is required to come to Delhi
physically for participating in the mediation proceedings, she will
be entitled to reimbursement of costs towards travelling, boarding
and lodging, which we quantify at Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand)
per visit. The same be deposited by the petitioner into the bank
account of the respondent no.1-wife or into the bank account of her
close relative, preferably her father, if she does not have a
personal bank account in her name, at least four days prior to the

We have heard learned Solicitor General appearing
for the State of Manipur; learned senior counsel appearing
for the fourth respondent; and also learned counsel for
the petitioner(s).
By  order  dated  24.09.2026,  we  had  observed  in
paragraph 5 as under:
“Till the disposal of the Writ Petition on
merits by the learned Single Judge, the respondents
shall maintain status quo.”
It  is  submitted  by  learned  Solicitor  General
appearing  for  the  respondent(s)-State  as  well  as  by
learned senior counsel appearing for the fourth respondent
in the Special Leave Petition(s) that even prior to the
date of passing of the order by this Court, on 22.09.2026
and 23.09.2026 work orders had already been issued to the
fourth respondent. Therefore, the observation aforesaid at
paragraph 5 of the order dated 24.09.2026 creates an
uncertainty inasmuch as the direction to maintain status
quo would imply that despite the work orders being issued
to the fourth respondent in the Special Leave Petition(s),
they cannot proceed with the work.
In the circumstances, we observe that in view of the
work orders being issued, the fourth respondent herein is
at liberty to carry on the work in terms of the said work
orders subject to result of the Writ Petition filed by the
petitioner(s) herein.

petitioner and Mr. Abhishek Pandey, learned counsel for
the State.
2. The  present  petition  calls  in  question  the

--- Page 364 ---
2
correctness of the order  dated 09-07-2026 in MCRC
No.6120/2026 passed by the High Court of Chhattisgarh
at Bilaspur. By the said order, the petitioner has been
denied the benefit of bail in connection with FIR/Crime
No.24/2024 registered with Kerlapal Police Station,
District  Sukuma,  Chhattisgarh,  for  the  offences
punishable under Section  20(b)(II)(C) of the Narcotic
Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (for short,
‘NDPS Act’).
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the
petitioner is in custody since 09.10.2024 and has
undergone  two  years  in  custody  as  on  date;  that
independent recovery witness(es) have not supported the
prosecution’s story; that still the State proposes to
examine nine more witnesses and the trial is likely to
take some time to conclude.
4. Learned counsel for the State defence the impugned
order.
5. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of
the  case;  the  period  already  undergone  by  the
petitioner; keeping in mind the liberty under Article
21 of the Constitution of India and bearing in mind the
principles of Section 37 of the NDPS Act, we are
inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
6. Accordingly, we direct that petitioner shall be
enlarged on bail subject to the satisfaction of the
concerned Trial Court in connection with the aforesaid

--- Page 365 ---
3
FIR/Crime and for the offences mentioned hereinabove.
7. The Special Leave Petition is disposed of in the
above terms.

disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
MISCELLANEOUS APPLICATION DIARY NO.1730/2023
IN
C.A. NO.  8047/2022
YOGEGOWDA(D) TR.LRS.                               APPLICANT(S)
                                VERSUS
CHANNEGOWDA (D) THR.LRS..                          RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. The applications for setting aside the abatement and for
substitution are allowed.
2. Cause title be amended accordingly. 
3. The present miscellaneous application has been filed
seeking  recall  of  judgment  dated  01.11.2022  in  Civil  Appeal
No.8047/2027 by the applicants, who were the respondents therein.
Aggrieved by the disposal of the appeal in view of a Memorandum of
Compromise dated 18.10.2022, the applicants are before this Court.
4. We have heard the learned counsel appearing for the
parties. 
5. Admittedly, the applicants being party-respondent(s) in
the Civil Appeal, though did not appear before this Court, were not
made parties to the Memorandum of Compromise. 

--- Page 373 ---
2
6. The compromise is binding on the other parties in the
Civil Appeal, as they were a party to it. The difficulty that
arises is that it cannot be given effect to unless the applicant(s)
agree  upon  the  terms  of  Memorandum  of  Compromise.  As  the
applicant(s) were not a party to the memorandum of compromise and
hence, they do not agree with the terms agreed upon thereunder.
7. In such view of the matter, we have no other option
except to set aside the judgment dated 01.11.2022, which leads to
setting aside the compromise inter se parties qua the share of the
applicant(s). 
8. Accordingly, the order dated 01.11.2022 stands set aside
and the appeal stands restored to its original file. 
9. IA No. 8057/2023 stands allowed and the Miscellaneous
Application stands disposed of.
    
  ……………………………………………………………………J.
  [M.M. SUNDRESH]
        ……………………………………………………………………J.
      [PRASANNA B. VARALE]
NEW DELHI;
25th SEPTEMBER, 2026

Jharkhand submits that respondent-State of Jharkhand

5. Though the incident relating to the death of the

evidence.  We  would  like  to  examine  the  various
circumstances  leading  to  the  conviction  of  the

6. In the meanwhile, as per the custody certificate
dated 19.11.2025, appellant had undergone 13 years 04
months 17 days of actual incarceration and with
remission, it was more than 17 years. Therefore, as
of today, actual incarceration would be more than 14
years.
7. That being the position, we suspend the sentence
awarded to the appellant and direct that he shall be
released on bail on usual terms and conditions.
8. Registry to requisition records of the Trial
Court as well as of the High Court.
9. List the Appeal for hearing in due course.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner.
2. The petitioner is the de-facto complainant. He is aggrieved by
the Order passed by the High Court releasing the Respondent No.1
(original accused) on bail. 
3. The  Respondent  No.1  has  been  charged  with  the  offence
punishable under the Arms Act. Insofar as the other co-accused are
concerned, they have been charged for the offence punishable
under Section 302 of the IPC i.e. the murder. 
4. We are of the view that there is no good ground for us to
cancel the bail granted by the High Court to the Respondent No.1.
5. We  are  informed  at  this  stage  that  the  petitioner  has
questioned the legality and validity of the order framing charge
against the Respondent No.1 before us. Let this challenge be looked
into by the Additional Sessions Judge, Narnaul District, State of
Haryana, without being influenced in any manner by any of the
observations made by the High Court in its impugned Order.
6. With the aforesaid, this petition stands disposed of.
7. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.

          UPON hearing the counsel, the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
Counter  affidavit  filed  by  the  State  of  Uttar  Pradesh
discloses  the  past  criminal  cases  registered  against  the
1

--- Page 631 ---
SLP(Crl.) No. 8278/2026
petitioner.  However, only some of those cases have been disclosed
in the special leave petition.  
Though the learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner
would state that the cases left out were, thereafter, referred to
in the rejoinder affidavit, we are of the opinion that the same
would not suffice as a litigant who approaches the Court is
expected to do so with clean hands, that is, by disclosing all the
material facts.
In the light of the law laid down by this Court in “Munnesh
vs. State of Uttar Pradesh” 1,  the failure to disclose the full
details of the past criminal cases registered against him is fatal
to  the  petitioner’s  case.  The  special  leave  petition  is,
accordingly, dismissed on that short ground.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

          UPON hearing the counsel, the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
Counter affidavit filed by the respondents, State of Madhya
Pradesh,  discloses  three  past  criminal  antecedents  of  the
petitioner, out of which he was acquitted in two.  However, the
third case, which is wrongly mentioned as First Information Report
(FIR) No. 85/2005 is actually FIR No. 85/2025 and is stated to be
at the stage of examination of the prosecution witnesses.  
1

--- Page 635 ---
SLP(Crl.) No. 4042/2026
Though the petitioner filed a rejoinder, taking advantage of
the mistake made in the counter affidavit, where the third FIR was
shown as pertaining to the year 2005, there is no denial of the
fact that FIR No. 85/2025 in relation to the offences mentioned in
the counter affidavit is pending at the stage of examination of the
prosecution witnesses.
In the light of the law laid down by this Court in “Munnesh
vs. State of Uttar Pradesh” 1, failure to disclose such details is
fatal to the petitioner’s case.  The special leave petition is,
accordingly, dismissed on that short ground.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
(DEEPAK GUGLANI)                                (PREETI SAXENA)
